articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas got pwned and schools nationwide are scrambling while kids celebrate an unexpected homework reprieve. Sometimes ransomware groups accidentally do public service.

articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft drops 167 vulnerabilities like it's a Black Friday sale, including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer.' Patch Tuesday or die Wednesday, folks.

articles.title: Milestone 1.0.0 Release of APK Downloader `apkeep` Powers Research on Android Apps
articles.summary: Russian military hackers turned routers into token-harvesting piñatas, because apparently even Office 365 auth tokens aren't safe from Putin's keyboard warriors. Your Linksys is now a Kremlin asset.

articles.title: After Replacing TeamPCP Malware, 'PCPJack' Steals Cloud Secrets
articles.summary: NSA whistleblower Binney's 'turnkey totalitarian state' warning hits harder than ever as surveillance infrastructure waits for the next authoritarian to flip the switch. Democracy dies in darkness, but authoritarianism thrives in metadata.

articles.title: Hackers ate my homework: Educational SaaS Canvas down after cyberattack
articles.summary: Zuckerberg pulls the ultimate privacy rug-pull, abandoning Instagram E2E encryption to peek at your DMs again. Meta's commitment to privacy has the durability of a Facebook promise.

articles.title: Ivanti EPMM CVE-2026-6973 RCE Under Active Exploitation Grants Admin-Level Access
articles.summary: Linux kernel gets a new unpatched privilege escalation bug dubbed 'Dirty Frag' because apparently 'Copy Fail' wasn't dramatic enough. Root access for everyone!

articles.title: Morning Minute: Morgan Stanley Is Coming for Coinbase
articles.summary: Ivanti's EPMM gets pwned through CVE-2026-6973 while attackers are already in the wild collecting admin privileges like Pokémon cards. Patch now or cry later.

articles.title: Finding the Vulnerability in Action: Composer Max Aruj on Scoring Netflix’s Man on Fire
articles.summary: Palo Alto's firewall zero-day got hammered by state-sponsored hackers for a full month before anyone noticed. The irony of security companies getting owned never gets old.

articles.title: Risky Business #836 -- You can't patch the bugpocalypse
articles.summary: Florida woman loses her life savings to SIM swappers in minutes, proving that your bank account is only as secure as your carrier's customer service training. Spoiler: it's terrible.

articles.title: GreenboneOS: April 2026 Threat Report: Mythos or Reality? Time to Find Out
articles.summary: Instructure hacker claims 280 million student records from 8,800 schools because apparently educational data is the new oil. Every term paper and lunch debt balance, now available on the dark web.
